newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL noon rubber little changed, currency concern.
newsitem.headline: KL noon rubber little changed, currency concern.

text.p: Rubber prices in Malaysia were little changed after firming in recent days on the back of the ringgit's weakness against the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
Little interest was seen this morning as buyers adopted a cautious stance over currency movements and Thai government's decision to default on taking delivery of rubber last week.
"We expect some inquiries from Far East, like China and South Korea, for SMR grades of rubber for nearby and forwards," a dealer said. "They may come in to ask for price levels."
Dealers offered SMR CV at 295 cents, SMR L at 275, SMR 5 at 254, SMR 10 at 249 and SMR 20 at 247 and latex at 191.
The easiness in the Tokyo market also cautioned most players, traders said, noting some covering from local dealers.
At noon, August RSS1 buyer was unchanged at 247.50 cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg and August SMR 20 buyer was up half a cent at 246.50.
Malaysia-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
